did_you_know.text: Did you know? Naaman is described as a great and honored man, a commander of the army and a mighty warrior—and yet he had leprosy. The text also notes that the Lord had given victory to Aram through him.
Did you know? The advice that led to Naaman’s healing came from an Israelite girl who had been captured and was serving Naaman’s wife. Despite her lowly position, her words had great influence.
Did you know? Naaman traveled to the land of Israel with a letter from the king of Aram and valuable gifts: ten talents of silver, six thousand pieces of gold, and ten sets of clothing.
Did you know? The king of Israel tore his clothes because he saw the king of Aram’s demand as an attempt to provoke him. He emphasized that only God can kill, give life, and heal leprosy.
Did you know? Elisha asked Naaman to come to him in order to prove to the king of Israel and everyone else that there was a prophet in Israel—not so that Elisha could present himself to the king.
Did you know? Elisha did not go out to meet Naaman himself. Instead, he sent a messenger with a simple instruction: wash seven times in the Jordan and be cleansed.

Did you know? Naaman became angry because he expected Elisha to perform an impressive ritual: come out to him, call on the name of the Lord, and wave his hand over the place affected by the leprosy. This shows that Naaman’s expectations differed from the way the prophet acted.

Did you know? It was Naaman’s servants who persuaded him to obey. They argued that if the prophet had told him to do something difficult, he would have done it—so how much more should he wash and be cleansed?
Did you know? After Naaman dipped himself in the Jordan seven times, his flesh was restored and became like the flesh of a young boy, and he was cleansed.

Did you know? Naaman wanted to give Elisha a gift as an expression of gratitude, but Elisha refused to accept anything and swore by the Lord that he would take nothing. Later in the chapter, the importance of this refusal becomes clear when Gehazi tries to obtain the gifts through deception.
